body:
<!--

  Please, DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! (unless instructed).

  and that the PR preview looks fine and does not include unrelated changes.

## Proposed change
<!-- 
    Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
    maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
    or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the 
    additional information section.
-->
This is a significant update to the NUT integration doc.  The current document lacks many of the sections expected for integrations (including not even meeting Bronze on the quality scale).  The current page is also moderately confusing/misleading and contains errors.  Significant cleanup is needed in reference to NUT command line instructions, NUT variables, and NUT commands.

Given the number of changes to bring this page up to date, I propose addressing this through this single PR.  A single PR allows reviewers to read and edit the full set of proposed changes in context of all of the other changes.  The alternative, reading one paragraph or section at a time, will likely be more difficult to review since it will require 12+ individual PRs.  If there is a need to split these apart, I can try to do so over the coming months.

The primary changes being addressed in this PR include:
- Clarify the need for a NUT server through the addition of new "Prerequisites" and "Setting up a NUT Server" sections.  The current instructions are not very clear on this general topic, which may explain the high number of how-to videos and step-by-step instructions.  Personally, I think it would be helpful to also include a tip referencing the HACS add-on but it seems there is a general preference away from those so I have not done so in this PR.  These sections reference the username and password required for the integration installation.
- Add missing docs-removal-instructions required for Bronze quality. The "Remove integration" section has been added.
- Add missing docs-installation-parameters for Silver quality.  The four installation parameters are now documented.
- Add missing docs-configuration-parameters required for Silver quality.  I saw the prior PR comments that sensor platforms should not document the scan_interval but I believe that likely only applied to YAML configuration.  The configuration parameter for the UI variable is now documented.
- Add missing docs-data-update for Gold quality. The "Data updates" section has been added.
- Add missing docs-examples for Gold quality. An example automation has now been provided for sending notifications when the battery state changes.
- Add missing docs-known-limitations for Gold quality.  The "Known limitations" section has been added to both describe functionality not supported by the integration and address frequent/repeat user issues.
- Add missing docs-supported-devices for Gold quality.  The "Supported devices" section has been added to reference the NUT hardware compatibility list.  I do not believe an "Unsupported devices" section is needed.
- Add missing docs-supported-functions for Gold quality.  A "Supported functionality" section was added with information about Sensors and Diagnostic Sensors.  Portions of the existing Device Actions were also moved into this section.  The new Sensors and Diagnostic Sensors sections add a complete list of available sensors.  The sensor lists include name, units and a short description.  The sensor with a blank description is ones that is not actually a valid NUT variable.  Added descriptions for certain sensors that are not listed as valid in nut-names.txt but are used by devices anyway. Reference to disabled sensors and instructions on how to enable such entities has also been added.  A link to the NUT manual on variables has also been added.
- Add missing docs-troubleshooting for Gold quality.  A "Troubleshooting" section has been added.  Given the recurring questions about the HACS NUT add-on, I suggest adding a short section regarding the add-on with a specific reference to the hostname (without documenting the actual hostname per the prior PRs requesting such information not be included in these docs).  I also propose moving several existing sections into troubleshooting guides since they are not required to use the integration and create more confusion than clarity.  The sections moved include (i) credentials/permissions, (ii) using NUT `upsc` for listing variables, and (iii) using NUT `upscmd` for listing commands.  Since the existing docs provided NUT configuration to help users with user credentials, I hae added one for the HACS NUT add-on as well.  Finally, given the meaningful number of users using the HACS add-on, I suggest providing an advanced troubleshooting section for accessing the docker container command line.  Including this in the documentation is likely worth of debate.  I note that one other integration provides similar instructions.  This is an area of frequent questions from users in Issues and Community posts.

A few additional changes to note:
- Add glossary markup for term "integration" on first use.
- Add glossary markup for term "automations" on first use.
- Expand applications of NUT to include PDUs and other devices to better align with the underlying NUT package.
- Added links to NUT's variables documentation.

I recognize the large number of changes and welcome improvements.

author: schoenwaldnils
body:
This PR implements a release workflow using [changeset](https://github.com/changesets/changesets)

resolves #3 

# Workflow: 
### 1. local
  - make changes
  - run `npx changeset` decide on scope and message
  - push to origin
### 2. PR
  - create PR
  - [changeset bot](https://github.com/apps/changeset-bot) checks for changesets
  - dev merges PR
### 3. Release PR
  - workflow release.yml runs on merge to main
  - job `Create changesets PR or Publish` is run, sees the changesets
  - creates (or updates) the Release PR
  - user/dev desides to publish/release and merges this PR
### 4. Release
  - workflow release.yml runs on merge to main
  - job `Create changesets PR or Publish` is run, this time does not see changesets and runs the `publish` command
  - git tag and git release is created and published
  - since this git release only has the 'source code' assests we manually add the plugin assets with `Upload Release Asset`


## ToDo:
@msakowski
  - [x] since we doesn't need to trigger another workflow (like I did in my last project using changesets) the bot user and its token can be removed from the repo again
  - [x] but we need the [changeset bot](https://github.com/apps/changeset-bot) to test the PRs for changesets. (the workflow works either way. But it is nice to have a reminder to add a changeset to the PR)

author: itsnickbarry
body:
This PR includes the following:
* Storage libraries have been moved to `contracts/storage/`.
* Where possible, storage libraries are named based on their underlying ERC.
* Closely related modules now share storage libraries.  This could save gas for reasons described [here](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7201#rationale).  Layouts that relate to multiple ERCs default to the most common (`ERC2612` variables are stored in the `ERC20` layout).
* Names added to storage library mapping keys and values.

Should storage gaps be added within `Layout` structs in order to separate groups of related variables?

Is a particular naming convention needed for non-ERC storage layouts?

author: seanturner
body: David noted in erratum 8137 that no hash algorithm was specified with id-alg-noSignature algorithm in Appendix C. RFC 6402 fixed this by defining sa-noSignature; it defines the hash algorithm as mda-sha1. RFC 6402's ASN.1 module is now in the I-D, so all that is really left is to say what that hash algorithm is in Appendix C. This is the PR for that.

author: falolatoluwalase8
body:
## Overview
This PR implements a simplified decentralized microfinance platform using Clarity smart contracts. The platform enables community-based lending with social collateral, transparent repayment tracking, and credit history building.

## Components

### 1. Loan Application Contract
- Manages borrower requests and loan terms
- Allows users to submit loan applications
- Provides admin functions to approve or reject applications
- Maintains a record of all loans

### 2. Group Guarantee Contract
- Implements social collateral through community groups
- Allows users to create and join lending groups
- Enables group members to provide guarantees for loans
- Requires at least 3 guarantors before a loan can be activated

### 3. Repayment Tracking Contract
- Monitors loan payments
- Tracks payments made and total payments required
- Provides functions to mark loans as defaulted when necessary
- Updates loan status when fully repaid

### 4. Credit History Contract
- Builds financial reputation for borrowers
- Maintains borrower profiles with loan history
- Updates credit scores based on repayment behavior
- Provides a transparent record of financial activity

## Technical Details

### Smart Contract Architecture
- Simplified data structures for better readability
- Clear error codes for consistent handling
- Proper authorization checks throughout
- Minimal dependencies between contracts

### Testing
- Comprehensive test suite using Vitest
- Tests cover all major functions and error conditions
- Mocking approach simulates blockchain interactions

## Deployment Instructions
1. Deploy the contracts in the following order:
   - Credit History Contract
   - Loan Application Contract
   - Group Guarantee Contract
   - Repayment Tracking Contract
2. Set the contract references in the Credit History Contract
3. Initialize the platform with default parameters

### New Features:
* Added `restaurantConfigRouter` and `analyticsRouter` to the application and included their respective routes (`functions/app.js`). [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-46e1b126f0343553285a6407d93e9f98573a900c57f3e31d6d52a37a86522176R18-R24) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-46e1b126f0343553285a6407d93e9f98573a900c57f3e31d6d52a37a86522176L48-R59)

[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-14b75ab093252b9744cee9c736714f5303b1a0fe7a14691ccec0042def075c91L134-R134) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-14b75ab093252b9744cee9c736714f5303b1a0fe7a14691ccec0042def075c91L147-R147) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-14b75ab093252b9744cee9c736714f5303b1a0fe7a14691ccec0042def075c91L156-R156) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-14b75ab093252b9744cee9c736714f5303b1a0fe7a14691ccec0042def075c91L165-R171) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-14b75ab093252b9744cee9c736714f5303b1a0fe7a14691ccec0042def075c91R180-R198)

body:
# User Deletion Performance Optimization

## Problem
Users cannot be deleted from the auth table due to incomplete implementation of the deletion process and performance issues with the Supabase Edge functions.

## Solution
- Implemented queue-based deletion system for better reliability
- Added timeout handling to prevent Edge function timeouts
- Optimized SQL functions for better performance
- Added comprehensive error handling and logging
- Created performance metrics tracking
- Added tests for user deletion functionality

### Queue-Based Deletion System
- Created a `deletion_queue` table to store pending user deletions
- Implemented a new Edge function `process_deletion_queue` to handle deletions asynchronously
- Added retry mechanism with configurable retry count
- Implemented health check endpoint to monitor queue status

### Timeout Handling
```typescript
// Set a timeout for the request
const timeoutPromise = new Promise<never>((_, reject) => {
  setTimeout(() => reject(new Error('Operation timed out')), 25000) // 25 seconds timeout
});

// Wrap the operation in a race with the timeout
await Promise.race([
  processUserDeletion(c, oldRecord),
  timeoutPromise,
]);
```

### SQL Optimizations
- Optimized the `delete_user` SQL function with more efficient queries
- Created a separate `get_sole_admin_orgs` function to improve query performance
- Used Common Table Expressions (CTEs) for better query performance
```sql
WITH sole_admin_orgs AS (
    SELECT org_id 
    FROM org_users
    WHERE user_id = v_user_id 
    AND user_right = 'super_admin'
    AND org_id NOT IN (
        SELECT org_id 
        FROM org_users
        WHERE user_right = 'super_admin' 
        AND user_id != v_user_id
    )
)
SELECT array_agg(org_id) INTO v_user_orgs FROM sole_admin_orgs;
```

### Performance Metrics
- Added a `record_performance_metric` function to track deletion performance
- Implemented metrics for deletion duration, success rate, and queue status
- Added structured logging with request IDs for better traceability

## Testing
- Added automated tests for the user deletion process
- Implemented retry logic in tests to handle asynchronous operations
- Added helper functions for safer RPC and query operations

Fixes #1072

This pull request includes changes to the `getUpcomingEventsTool` and `structured-data-parser` to enhance the functionality of filtering events. The primary addition is the inclusion of a required `searchTerm` parameter to filter events by name or description, even if the term is an empty string.

Enhancements to event filtering:

* [`src/utils/ai-tools/get-upcoming-events-tool.ts`](diffhunk://#diff-3916433c5c22fd780823fd38b5bff90910884c50c2794b566701aeb0a321f879L55-R60): Made the `searchTerm` parameter required but allowed it to be an empty string. Updated the client-side filtering logic to check if the `searchTerm` is provided and not empty before applying the filter. author: binarycounter
body:
# New Port for Open Hexagon

Needs at least Westonpack 0.2.6 due to the new GLES 1.1 mode it offers. Panfrost does not seem to support GLES 1.1, so there is a OpenGL 2 build included aswell. The script will use it when needed. 
The game is very slightly modified to change the default keybinds and to remove controller support. 
Game assets are not included, they can be obtained by buying the game on Steam or Itch, or for free by downloading them from the developers Github. Links for this are included in the readme. Buying on Steam is highly encouraged for custom levels through workshop (instructions are in the readme) and to support the developer.


## Game Information
- **Title**: Open Hexagon
- **URL**: https://vittorioromeo.com/openhexagon.html

## Submission Requirements

### CFW Tests
Ensure your game has been tested on all major CFWs:
- [X] AmberELEC
- [X] ArkOS
- [X] ROCKNIX (Panfrost / Mali)
- [X] muOS
- [X] Knulli

### Resolution Tests
Test all major resolutions:
- [X] 480x320
- [X] 640x480
- [~] 720x720 (RGB30) (Resolution only tested on PC, scales well. Told on Discord to PR anyway)
- [X] Higher resolutions (e.g., 1280x720)

## File Structure
- Your port should have the following structure:
  - portname/
    - port.json
    - README.md
    - screenshot.jpg
    - cover.jpg
    - gameinfo.xml
    - Port Name.sh
    - portname/
      - <portfiles here>

## Additional Resources
For an in-depth guide on creating a pull request, refer to: [PortMaster Game Packaging Guide](https://portmaster.games/packaging.html#creating-a-pull-request)

author: jmoseley
body:
## Summary
- Add option to select AI assistant packages during project creation
- Add support for Claude, Cursor, Cline, and Windsurf assistants
- Add `--skip-ide-rules` flag to bypass assistant selection
- Add `--ide-rules` flag to specify assistants directly (e.g., `--ide-rules claude,cursor`)
- Remove cursor rules from TypeScript template as they're now installed via the package
- Update documentation in quickstart guide to explain AI assistant integration options
- Fix linting issues

## Testing
- Built and verified locally with non-interactive (`--ai-assistants`) mode
- Added tests for AI assistant integration in create-gensx
- Fixed linting issues and ensured all tests pass
- Checked content consistency across all AI assistant templates

This PR completes the integration of our AI assistant packages into the project creation flow, allowing users to add AI assistant integration right from the start.

Closed #450

Reimplementation of the tab system to work with multiple units simultaneously. 
The main enhancements include:

- Persistent Action Bar: The "new unit" and "load unit" buttons remain visible and accessible regardless of how many tabs are open. Two positioning modes are supported: trailing mode (default, after the last tab) or fixed mode (right edge of the tab pane)
- Detachable Tabs: Units can be popped out into separate windows
- Tab Sorting: Tabs can be reordered via drag and drop
- Visual Feedback: Ghost tab visualization during drag operations provides clear feedback

These features have been implemented in two places:
- The main unit tabs in MegaMekLabTabbedUI
- The detail tabs within each unit editor (Structure, Equipment, Quirks, Preview, etc.)

body:
以下の修正をChapter5に追加し、P2P通信を扱うステップ3を完成させました。

主な変更内容
	1.	P2Pの最小実装
	•	サーバーモードでノード間の接続待受、および受信スレッドを追加
	•	クライアントモードでサーバーへの接続＋送信用スレッドを追加
	2.	メッセージ形式
	•	"BLOCK:" プレフィックス＋JSON という簡易的な形式でブロックデータを送受
	•	受信側はparseMessageで判別し、parseBlockJsonを経由してブロックをチェインに取り込み
	3.	動作確認
	•	--listen <port> でサーバーモード、--connect <host:port> でクライアントモード
	•	クライアントコンソールにBLOCK:{"index":2,"nonce":777}などと入力し送信 → サーバでブロックが追加される

今後のステップでは、より複雑なブロック検証やトランザクションリレー、マルチスレッド/非同期処理の活用も追記予定。

author: yersiniapestis899
body:
## 🧪 システム的問題解決アプローチ

### 🔍 問題分析フレームワーク
エラーメッセージ`"Could not find the 'last_saved' column of 'quizzes' in the schema cache"`は、TypeScript型定義と実際のデータベーススキーマ間の構造的不一致を明示しています。この不具合は前回の型定義更新（Quiz型にuser_answers、score、last_saved、last_playedプロパティを追加）後に発生し、対応するデータベーススキーマの変更が実施されなかったことに起因します。

### 📊 解決戦略の多層構造

**1. データモデルの二重構造化**
- 完全なオブジェクト（ローカルストレージとメモリ用）と、互換性のあるオブジェクト（Supabase用）を明確に分離
- この分離により型システムの整合性を維持しつつ、実データベースとの互換性を確保

**2. エラー診断の精緻化**
- エラー発生時の詳細情報（details, hint, codeなど）を包括的に記録
- 根本原因の効率的な特定とトラブルシューティングを容易化

**3. データ永続化の堅牢性向上**
- インメモリストレージの更新ロジック最適化（既存エントリの更新または新規追加）
- Supabase応答データとローカル完全データの統合によるデータ一貫性の強化

## 🛠️ 実装詳細マトリクス

| コンポーネント | 変更前 | 変更後 | 改善効果 |
|-------------|--------|--------|---------|
| 保存オブジェクト構造 | 単一構造 | 二重構造（完全/互換） | スキーマ不一致の解消 |
| エラーハンドリング | 基本的な記録 | 詳細診断情報の記録 | トラブルシューティング効率化 |
| インメモリ更新 | 常に追加 | 更新または追加 | データ整合性向上 |
| 応答データ処理 | そのまま返却 | ローカルデータとの統合 | 機能的一貫性確保 |

## 📈 期待される成果

1. クイズ保存機能の完全な機能回復
2. データベースとクライアント間のシームレスな連携
3. 将来的なスキーマ更新が必要な場合の移行パス確立

### 長期戦略的展望
今後の機能追加時には、以下の優先順序に従うことで同様の問題を防止できます：
1. データベーススキーマの拡張
2. バックエンドコードの適応
3. フロントエンドモデルの更新

このアプローチにより、モデルとスキーマの一貫性を確保し、システムの全体的な安定性を向上させることができます。

author: ash-bergs
body:
## Context 

In our last body of work we migrated the Tasks and Tags *back* to indexDB, managing them locally for a snappy UI and reduced PUT/POST/UPDATE/DELETE requests. This was done to drive TrekBit to be an offline-first tool, allowing a user to keep their data off of databases they don't control. 

But this has left us with no mechanism for informing the database we host in RDS about the current tasks and tags a user has, and allowing them to sync between devices. 

## Changes 

- Adds `syncTasks` method to the Task Service and Store 
- Adds `syncStatus` column to Tasks maintained in the local indexdb, allowing `new` | `pending` | `deleted` | `synced` values 
- Replaces most old api/tasks routes with a single PUT handler for syncing, while keeping old routes commented for reference: 
  - First checks for newly added tasks - `new` syncStatus - adds to DB
  - Second checks for updated tasks - `pending` syncStatus - `update` items in DB
  - Third checks for deleted tasks - `deleted` syncStatus - `delete` items in DB
  - Once this route returns with response.ok, the Task Service handles updating index db, marking new and updated items as `synced` and fully removing deleted items 
- Adds shadcn and ToolTip
- Adds "Sync Status" button with tool tip 

These changes allow for one-way syncing, triggered manually via a button. Future iterations may introduce background syncing or automated triggers.

## Testing 

1. `docker compose up` && `npm run dev`
2. Remove `disabled` on Sync Status button in TaskToolbar.tsx 
3. Add some tasks (no tag) 
4. Check your application data - tasks should appear with syncStatus property 
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e732f45f-b2be-46db-96fb-5f91e86eb888)
5. Run syncing by clicking Sync Status
6. Refresh application data to view changes 
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cfaed795-f954-4f71-afa1-c69dd919852a)

author: gitenghar
body:
~ 2003 であれば 税抜き価格を 2004 ~であれば 税込価格を表示したい

### Bad Plactis UNION

```sql
SELECT item_name, year , price_tax_ex AS price FROM shop WHERE 2003 >= year
UNION ALL
SELECT item_name, year , price_tax_in AS price FROM shop WHERE  year >= 2004
```

実行計画を取るとこうなる

フルスキャンが2回走っており 補足で extraが using whereなので where文にもindex使われておらず、間違いなく遅い計算になってる

```bash
mysql> EXPLAIN SELECT item_name, year , price_tax_ex AS price FROM shop WHERE 2003 >= year
    -> UNION ALL
    -> SELECT item_name, year , price_tax_in AS price FROM shop WHERE  year >= 2004
    -> ;
+----+-------------+-------+------------+------+---------------+------+---------+------+------+----------+-------------+
| id | select_type | table | partitions | type | possible_keys | key  | key_len | ref  | rows | filtered | Extra       |
+----+-------------+-------+------------+------+---------------+------+---------+------+------+----------+-------------+
|  1 | PRIMARY     | shop  | NULL       | ALL  | NULL          | NULL | NULL    | NULL |   16 |    33.33 | Using where |
|  2 | UNION       | shop  | NULL       | ALL  | NULL          | NULL | NULL    | NULL |   16 |    33.33 | Using where |
+----+-------------+-------+------------+------+---------------+------+---------+------+------+----------+-------------+
2 rows in set, 1 warning (0.00 sec)
```

### Good Plactis CASE

```sql
SELECT item_name, year,
    CASE WHEN 2003 >= year THEN price_tax_ex
         WHEN year >= 2004 THEN price_tax_in ELSE NULL END AS price
FROM shop;

```

実行計画をとると 1回のフルスキャンで完結しおり、WHERE句も使っていないので検索の手間もない
```bash
mysql> EXPLAIN SELECT item_name, year,
    ->     CASE WHEN 2003 >= year THEN price_tax_ex
    ->          WHEN year >= 2004 THEN price_tax_in ELSE NULL END AS price
    -> FROM shop;
+----+-------------+-------+------------+------+---------------+------+---------+------+------+----------+-------+
| id | select_type | table | partitions | type | possible_keys | key  | key_len | ref  | rows | filtered | Extra |
+----+-------------+-------+------------+------+---------------+------+---------+------+------+----------+-------+
|  1 | SIMPLE      | shop  | NULL       | ALL  | NULL          | NULL | NULL    | NULL |   16 |   100.00 | NULL  |
+----+-------------+-------+------------+------+---------------+------+---------+------+------+----------+-------+
1 row in set, 1 warning (0.00 sec)
```

author: chadys
body:
My proposal to solve #1196

## What does this do
This will add additional url entries in the generated sitemap, one for each translated pages.
This will also add appropriate alternates markup for each url.
All this follows the [google specification](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/specialty/international/localized-versions#sitemap).

These additions to the sitemap will be automatically made if `WAGTAIL_I18N_ENABLED=True` in settings; a parameter in the view can also override that behaviour.

Docs and tests have been updated.

Seems to works well after testing on a dummy site.

## How is it done

I tried to optimise for database queries as well as memory consumption to answer the valid concerns raised in the issue.

The commit add one[^1] additional db query for each batch of pages to get every related translations.

In term of db queries: this scales by a constant factor with the number of queries that were already made by the view.
In term of memory: the consumption is larger by O(N) where N is the number of activated locales (assuming that every pages are translated).

[^1]: one is an approximation since `specific()` is called, it will be slightly more that that but still in one queryset

author: clackyai[bot]
body:
This PR initializes the development environment for the Go-Vue-Admin project, setting up necessary configurations for the Clacky cloud environment and updating the README.

#### Key Changes
- Configured the .1024 file with run and dependency commands for the Clacky environment.
- Updated the .gitignore file to exclude Clacky-related and frontend-related files.
- Translated the README.md file from Chinese to English while preserving formatting.

#### Rationale
These changes are essential for setting up a functional development environment within the Clacky cloud, ensuring proper dependency management, and facilitating a better understanding of the project for English-speaking developers.

#### Impact
These updates will streamline the development process in Clacky by pre-configuring the environment and preventing unnecessary files from being tracked in Git. The translated README will improve project accessibility.

author: willnet
body:
I created a method to help developers avoid accidentally loading Rails components without lazy loading when they build gems for extending Rails.

```ruby
A::NtiMannerKickCourse.monitor { require 'your_gem' }
```

By running this regularly in CI, you can make sure your gem is lazy loading Rails components properly.

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/sindresorhus/screenfull/compare/v5.2.0...v6.0.0)

##### Breaking

-   This package is now pure ESM. **Please [read this](https://gist.github.com/sindresorhus/a39789f98801d908bbc7ff3ecc99d99c).**
    -   If you cannot easily move to ESM. Just stay on version 5.2.0. It's stable and fine.
-   This package now uses modern JavaScript syntax. If you need support for older browsers, you need to transpile the code with Babel.
-   A minified version is no longer provided in the package. It's better to minify your project as a whole in your own build step.
-   `screenfull.element` is now `undefined` instead of `null` when there's no fullscreen element.
-   The `document` global is no longer polyfilled. If you run this package in a non-browser environment, it's up to you to polyfill required browser globals.

author: hakasapl
body:
This PR is intended to add a CS port for [Terrain Helper for ENB](https://www.nexusmods.com/skyrimspecialedition/mods/143149) as a feature.

**This PR is a draft as I haven't ironed out everything yet**

What works:
* Additional discrete parallax slots for terrain in unused slots `92-97` when read directly in `ExtendedMaterials.hlsli` show parallax correctly on landscape.
* All features of the original terrain helper including default terrain texture and EDID lookup
* PBR terrain doesn't break with this enabled, terrain helper functionality is ignored correctly

What doesn't work:
* Runtime detection of whether an extended slot is used for parallax or not (ie. whether the shader should use alpha of diffuse like normal or a discrete slot)
    * This is the main thing I'm stuck on. I think it has something to do with how the constant buffers are applied. Terrain helper lets the vanilla function setup the material in `BSLightingShader_SetupMaterial` but then afterwards adds the additional required slots. The original plugin did not need any constant buffers so this is new territory for me.
    * I do not see the constant buffer I defined show up in nsight, so the conditionals in `ExtendedMaterials.hlsli` always fails and it falls back to regular parallax from alpha of diffuse.
    * I've tried running `FlushPSConstantGroup` and `ApplyPSConstantGroup` to no avail. I don't think the buffer is being set.
    * My suspicion is that I need to control the whole material pipeline for terrain like PBR terrain does otherwise the buffers don't apply. If anyone has insight I would appreciate it!

Other notes:
* I had to move 2 hooks out of `TruePBR` class because terrain helper needs to hook them as well. I moved them to `Hooks.cpp` and both TruePBR functions and terrain helper functions are called.
* This feature adds a esp plugin as well which holds the default landscape texture set. Mods that use terrain helper override it and add it as a master.
* I will fix any CI checks and squash commits prior to marking this ready for review, just wanted to make this a PR so the diff is easy to view for others in the meantime.

author: danbev
body:
This commit adds the `--symlinks` option to the zip command used to create the xcframework zip file. This is necessary to create symlinks in the zip file. Without this option,  the Versions symlink is stored as a regular directory entry in the zip file, rather than as a symlink in the zip which causes the followig error in xcode:
```console
Couldn't resolve framework symlink for '/Users/danbev/work/ai/llama.cpp/tmp_1/build-apple/llama.xcframework/macos-arm64_x86_64/llama.framework/Versions/Current': readlink(/Users/danbev/work/ai/llama.cpp/tmp_1/build-apple/llama.xcframework/macos-arm64_x86_64/llama.framework/Versions/Current): Invalid argument (22)
```

Refs: https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/11996#issuecomment-2727026377

body:
# Pull Request Template

## Description

Intuition
The problem is about finding two vertical lines that can contain the most water. The key observation is that the area is determined by the smaller height among the two chosen lines and the distance between them.
To maximize the area, we should consider the widest possible container first and then move the pointers inward based on which height is smaller.

Approach
Two Pointers Approach:
We start with two pointers:
i at the leftmost index (0).
j at the rightmost index (n-1).
Compute the current area using:
area=(j−i)×min⁡(height[𝑖],height[𝑗])
area=(j−i)×min(height[i],height[j])
Update the maximum area if the new area is greater.
Move the pointer that has the smaller height:
If height[i] < height[j], increase i (move right).
Otherwise, decrease j (move left).
Repeat the process until i < j.
This approach ensures that we explore all possible containers efficiently.

author: ifosch
body:
This PR introduces an `appu` subcommand to APPU 2, with the same features as old `appu` program/container. This also introduces a first version for a container image for APPU 2.

This proposal takes one first step to replace old `appu` tooling with a new one. In theory, this could replace the [Edit and upload the audio file](https://github.com/EDyO/appu?tab=readme-ov-file#edit-and-upload-the-audio-file) step in the publishing pipeline.

Check out the commit messages for more information regarding:
* New subcommand features and tests added
* Changes in dependencies, caused by upgrading to Python 3.13
* Changes in selection of CI pipelines steps
* Trick added to prevent weird output, caused by pydub's not supporting Python 3.12+
* Tests and container usage.

Further work in this direction, pending discussions, could be:
* Replace `epidator`
* Replace `feedupdater`
* Replace `uploader`
* Include publishing Youtube to the tool
* Add a validation step
* Add more possible editions to master recording

author: aberdasher
body:
## Overview
This PR adds a new `/report` command that allows users to report match results directly from draft channels. It also introduces a significant improvement to our database access patterns by implementing a context manager and adding model-based query methods.

## Changes

### 1. New `/report` Command
- Added a slash command that lets users report their match results from any draft channel
- Command automatically finds the user's earliest unreported match
- Uses the existing `MatchResultSelect` UI component for consistent user experience

### 2. Database Access Improvements
- Added `db_session()` context manager to handle session lifecycle and transaction management
- Implemented model-based query methods:
  - `DraftSession.get_by_channel_id()`
  - `DraftSession.get_by_session_id()`
  - `DraftSession.is_user_participating()`
  - `MatchResult.find_unreported_for_user()`

### 3. Code Organization
- Refactored database operations to follow the Active Record pattern
- Reduced code duplication and boilerplate in database access
- Improved command structure with clearer separation of concerns

## Benefits
- **User Experience**: Players can now report match results directly from their team channels
- **Code Quality**: Database operations are now more consistent and have less boilerplate
- **Maintainability**: Database queries are centralized in model classes
- **Error Handling**: Improved transaction management with automatic commits/rollbacks

## Testing
The `/report` command needs to be tested with:
- Multiple users in a draft
- Non-draft channels
- Users not participating in drafts

author: oluwagbengaajayi
body:
## Overview
This PR implements a blockchain-based food bank distribution system using Clarity smart contracts on the Stacks blockchain with a Next.js frontend interface. The system aims to improve transparency, efficiency, and fairness in food distribution to those in need.

## Key Components

### Smart Contracts
**Inventory Management Contract**
   - Tracks available supplies based on donations
   - Monitors expiration dates to reduce waste
   - Controls inventory updates through admin permissions
   - Marks items as unavailable when allocated or expired

## Technical Implementation

- **Smart Contracts**: Written in Clarity with a focus on security and data integrity
- **Testing**: Comprehensive unit tests for all contracts using Vitest

## Benefits

1. **Transparency**: All donations and distributions are recorded on the blockchain
2. **Efficiency**: Smart contracts automate allocation and reduce administrative overhead
3. **Fairness**: Optimization algorithms ensure resources are distributed equitably
4. **Waste Reduction**: Expiration tracking helps prioritize distribution of soon-to-expire items
5. **Accountability**: Full audit trail of donations and distributions

## Future Enhancements

1. Integration with IoT devices for real-time inventory tracking
2. Implementation of more sophisticated optimization algorithms
3. Mobile application for on-site inventory management
4. Analytics dashboard for long-term trends and impact measurement
5. Integration with other charitable platforms and donation systems

Release notes
Package name: express
  • 5.0.0 - 2024-09-10

    Express v5.0.0

    🎉 Express v5 is finally here! 🎉

    After years of development, the long-awaited Express v5 has been officially released. This version focuses on simplifying the codebase, improving security, and dropping support for older Node.js versions to enable better performance and maintainability.

    For detailed information, please check out the official Express v5 release blog post.

    Most relevant details

    Major Changes in v5

    • Node.js version support: Dropped support for Node.js versions before v18.
    • Routing changes: Updated to path-to-regexp@8.x, removing sub-expression regex patterns for security reasons (ReDoS mitigation).
    • Promise support: Middleware can now return rejected promises, caught by the router as errors.
    • body-parser changes: Several improvements including the ability to customize urlencoded body depth and defaulting extended to false.
    • Deprecated API methods removed: Removed old, deprecated API method signatures from Express v3/v4.

    For a complete list of breaking changes and API deprecations, see the migration guide.

    Security Updates

    This release includes important security fixes, including improvements to prevent ReDoS attacks and mitigation for CVE-2024-45590. Full details can be found in the security release notes.

    Migration

    Be sure to check out our migration guide for instructions on how to update your applications from Express v4 to v5.

    Security Guidance

    For best practices, we recommend reviewing the Threat Model which outlines Express' approach to securing your applications, including tips for user input validation and other critical aspects.

    What's Changed

    • 4.19.2 Staging by @ wesleytodd in #5561
    • remove duplicate location test for data uri by @ wesleytodd in #5562
    • feat: document beta releases expectations by @ marco-ippolito in #5565
    • Cut down on duplicated CI runs by @ jonchurch in #5564

author: scribblemaniac
body:
It appears this is necessary to fix Pencil2D failing to start with XWayland. Running the Pencil2D Flatpak with `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=xcb` on Wayland (Debian 11.11.0 Gnome) results in an error such as:
```
qt.qpa.xcb: could not connect to display 
qt.qpa.plugin: From 6.5.0, xcb-cursor0 or libxcb-cursor0 is needed to load the Qt xcb platform plugin.
qt.qpa.plugin: Could not load the Qt platform plugin "xcb" in "" even though it was found.
This application failed to start because no Qt platform plugin could be initialized. Reinstalling the application may fix this problem.

Available platform plugins are: eglfs, linuxfb, minimal, minimalegl, offscreen, vkkhrdisplay, vnc, wayland-egl, wayland, xcb.
```
as reported by a user [here](https://discuss.pencil2d.org/t/cant-install-using-flatpak/9516/5).

Unfortunately I was not able to reproduce their other crash with Wayland, but a newer version of Qt may help with that too.

author: masahito-uwamichi
body:
This pull request includes updates to the `.github/workflows/run-main.yml` file to upgrade the Python version used in the workflow and make some adjustments to the setup and execution steps.

Changes to Python version:

* Updated the Docker image to use Python 3.12 instead of Python 3.10.
* Updated the `setup-python` action to use Python 3.12 instead of Python 3.10.

Adjustments to setup and execution steps:

* Changed the working directory for installing dependencies and running the script to `nook`.
* Simplified the `pip install` commands by removing the `nook/` prefix from the requirements files.
* Corrected the `REDDIT_CLIENT_ID` environment variable by removing the trailing `=`.

author: knowler
body:
Supersedes #4, #11

This pull request updates the URL structure in preparation for localization. It also introduces Rosetta as a translation mechanism. Translations are in `/translations/{lang}.json`. The keys are in English as that’s the primary codebase language.

Currently nothing is fully translated so I have a number of 307 temporary redirects in place until we complete that. The `/` route also redirects to `/en`, but I think in the future it should be a bilingual landing page for the project which will route folks into the correct localization of the site.

The next PR will be to get all of the strings into the translations files so we can start getting those translated.

Also, ideally, we’ll use the slugified constituency names for the provinces as well, however, right now it’s still using the member’s name as a slug.

author: opsiff
body:
mainline inclusion
from mainline-v6.11-rc1
category: performance

The current code loops over the psi_states only to call a helper which then resolves back to the action needed for each state using a switch statement. That is effectively creating a double indirection of a kind which, given how all the states need to be explicitly listed and handled anyway, we can simply remove. Both the for loop and the switch statement that is.

The benefit is both in the code size and CPU time spent in this function. YMMV but on my Steam Deck, while in a game, the patch makes the CPU usage go from ~2.4% down to ~1.2%. Text size at the same time went from 0x323 to 0x2c1.



Reviewed-by: Chengming Zhou <chengming.zhou@linux.dev>
Acked-by: Johannes Weiner <hannes@cmpxchg.org>
Link: https://lkml.kernel.org/r/20240625135000.38652-1-tursulin@igalia.com (cherry picked from commit 0ec208ce9834929769ace0e2a506106192d08069)

- Optimise psi_group_change function by removing unnecessary loop and switch statement.

# Context

Currently the test job and pvc are hardcoded. Any deviation from the standard storage class name will result in an error when deploying the chart.

# Proposal

* Make the test container optional and slightly configureable so we can specify the storageclass
* No-break change on the chart, defaults will simulate the original behavior

author: nopemanmchalt
body:
## About The Pull Request
This will remove duplicate and older GWTB outfits (named Blastwave `[clothing]`) from loadout. It was part of Skyrat coding. ~~However, what was done is essentially unticking the module folder and commenting out items in master file's loadout.~~
Nevermind, I forgot I could just override things.
Updates outfit to allow basic reskinning (just Default Purple, Red, Green, Blue and Yellow insignia colors). Don't ask me to make GAGS version.
This also adds outfit to clothesmate, special category... And ports ability to buy armored variants of trencher/GWTB coats from cargo imports as contraband.

author: liincu4n
body:
This pull request addresses performance bottlenecks and numerical stability issues in the `DOD250` audio plugin class. The changes improve real-time processing efficiency and ensure the solver behaves reliably under edge cases.

### Changes
1. **Performance Optimization in `processBlock`**  
   - **Problem**: Frequent recomputation of the `S` matrix (involving matrix inversion) in `processBlock` was inefficient, especially when `Z` changes were minor.
   - **Solution**: 
     - Added `S_cached` and `Z_last` properties to cache the scattering matrix `S` and track the last state of `Z`.
     - Replaced `sum([sum(...), sum(...)])` with `any()` for simpler and potentially faster condition checking.
     - Compute `S` only when `Z` changes significantly (using Frobenius norm), reducing redundant inversions.
   - **Impact**: Decreases CPU load during audio processing, making the plugin more suitable for real-time use.

2. **Numerical Stability in `processBlock`**  
   - **Problem**: The `while norm(p.v - p.v_old) >= p.tol_SLV` loop could run indefinitely if convergence fails, risking crashes or audio glitches.
   - **Solution**: 
     - Added `maxIter` property (default: 1000) to cap solver iterations.
     - Introduced an iteration counter and a warning if convergence isn’t achieved within `maxIter`.
   - **Impact**: Prevents infinite loops and provides feedback on solver issues, improving robustness.

### Modified Files
- `DOD250.m`: Updated class properties and `processBlock` method.

### Testing
- Verified with a sample audio input that the plugin still produces the expected overdrive effect.
- Confirmed that `S` updates only when necessary and the solver exits cleanly even under non-converging conditions.

author: louislelay
body:
# Description

This PR introduces a direct workflow environment for the Reach task. Currently, it only has a manager-based workflow, but having both options is seen as beneficial as mentioned in kellyguo11’s suggestion in issue https://github.com/isaac-sim/IsaacLab/issues/748.

I created this as a first step while working on the Jenga task. I believe this implementation can serve as a template for others interested in developing direct workflow environments for the "Help Needed" tasks, offering an easier starting point compared to the more complex setups already available.

Fixes https://github.com/isaac-sim/IsaacLab/issues/748

## Type of change

- New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- This change requires a documentation update

## Screenshots

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/10c51ac2-1a6c-47c8-ae19-17d6b38ec9ea

## Checklist

- [x] I have run the [`pre-commit` checks](https://pre-commit.com/) with `./isaaclab.sh --format`
- [x] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation
- [x] My changes generate no new warnings
- [ ] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works
- [x] I have updated the changelog and the corresponding version in the extension's `config/extension.toml` file
- [x] I have added my name to the `CONTRIBUTORS.md` or my name already exists there

author: ophthal
body:
fixes #8151 

When the Eye Form loads it will display the Form as the authID/current user prefers (based on the last time they used the form) - which panels are open by default, which are closed, minus or plus cylinder, Draw/quick picks panel open, whole sections of exam hidden, etc.  Some people will never use the Neuro section, so it is hidden. Others want the Retina Draw panel to display by default, others will want the Glaucoma Fee Sheet to display on opening the form.  Each time a panel is changed, that UI choice is stored as the current preference and subsequent Eye Forms will open/display the same way for that user.  This change fixes a bug where the RETINA section was not honoring preferences, because it was mis-labelled as POSTSEG.  Now all is well.

body:
This pull request includes significant updates to the `cashier_backend` module, focusing on enhancements to data structures, API modifications, and the addition of comprehensive tests. The most important changes include the introduction of new data types, adjustments to existing types, and the addition of new constants and tests.

### Data Structure Enhancements:
* Added `MetadataValue` and `TransactionDto` types to `src/cashier_backend/cashier_backend.did` and `src/cashier_backend/src/core/action/types.rs`. These new types provide more detailed metadata and transaction information. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-2f30a925cb727ba9384a9e0ef4bc5293134e001e8af491ec6b4cd29963469ae2L81-R87) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-2f30a925cb727ba9384a9e0ef4bc5293134e001e8af491ec6b4cd29963469ae2R113-R119) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-7de41e21ace340de022d09aa4f266d04d4073fa88a7d173ab133e214ad5c8985L84-R120)
* Updated `IntentDto` to include `transactions` and replaced `TypeMetdataValue` with `MetadataValue`. This improves the representation of intent-related data. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-2f30a925cb727ba9384a9e0ef4bc5293134e001e8af491ec6b4cd29963469ae2L81-R87) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-7de41e21ace340de022d09aa4f266d04d4073fa88a7d173ab133e214ad5c8985L84-R120)

### API Modifications:
* Changed return types and parameters for several service functions to better align with the new data structures. This includes updates to `trigger_transaction` and `update_action` methods in `src/cashier_backend/src/core/action/api.rs`. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-ee28a9ecbf6448ec11b80f1e81a66b4419e6ed8e56c3af15f9eedd3048c7ee2dL78-R48) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-ee28a9ecbf6448ec11b80f1e81a66b4419e6ed8e56c3af15f9eedd3048c7ee2dL99-R71)
* Removed the `create_action` method from `src/cashier_backend/src/core/action/api.rs` as part of the refactoring process.

### New Constants:
* Introduced new constants for intent labels in `src/cashier_backend/src/constant/mod.rs` to standardize intent types.

### Test Additions:
* Added comprehensive tests for the `LinkApi` in `src/cashier_backend/src/core/__tests__/link/mod.rs` to ensure the correctness of the process action logic. These tests cover various scenarios including valid user actions, existing actions, user not found, invalid action types, and insufficient balance cases.
* Included a new test module reference in `src/cashier_backend/src/core/__tests__/mod.rs` to organize the tests better.

These changes collectively enhance the robustness, readability, and maintainability of the `cashier_backend` module.

Add envvar REACT_APP_USE_EXPOSE_HEADERS to add the 'Access-Control-Expose-Headers' header calling the backend (defaults to be off) [GS-15].
Configure lines per page in the CRUD editor: save and restore it from the LocalStorage. Defaults to 30 (previous was 5) [GS-185].

Add getErrorDetail() function to get the error details from the error object [GS-15].
Add getUuidV4() function to generate a UUID v4 [GS-15].
Add getContentTypeFromHeadersOrFilename() function to get the content type from the headers or filename [GS-15].
Add copy_ssl_certs Makefile target to copy the SSL certificates generated in the backend to the frontend [GS-198].
Add setupTests.js to fix jest test with "react-router-dom" to v7 [GS-199].

Add the "TARGET_DIR" (defaults to "public") and "BASE_DIR" (defaults to ".") parameters to the "build_copy_images.sh" script to copy the images to the "public" directory [GS-188].

### Changes
GCE_RFC and class_name_constants code cleanup.
convertId() function moved from db.service.jsx to id.utilities.jsx [GS-185].

isBinaryFileType() receives additional contentType parameter to get the content type from the headers or filename [GS-15].
getFilenameFromContentDisposition() verifies if the content disposition header contains a filename with or without quotes [GS-15].
Install vite, webpack or react-app-rewired dependencies running run_app_frontend.sh according to the RUN_METHOD env var [GS-198].
Remove vite, webpack and react-app-rewired dependencies running npm_publish.sh [GS-198].

React Router updated from "^v6.18.0" to "^v7.5.3" [GS-199].
Default node version upgraded to 20 in ".nvmrc" [GS-199].
Tailwind CSS updated from "^v3.4.9" to "^v4.1.5" [GS-112].
Add *.ts, *.tsx and ./index.html files to tailwind.config.js [GS-112].
All debugging flags turned off.

Fix the net:ERR_CERT_AUTHORITY_INVALID error in GenericSuite FE/BE using the https protocol [GS-198].
Fix the create_ssl_certs Makefile target to effectively call the backend self-signed SSL certificates creation [GS-198].
Fix the React Router v7 Future Flag Warning by upgrading "react-router-dom" to v7 [GS-199].

author: koltunovoleg
body:
Create components

**Counter**
A component that renders a numeric value and two buttons: one to decrement the value by 1, another to increment the value by 1.
The component should take an initial value in a property.
The component should be written using EcmaScript classes syntax, the `render` method should use `React.createElement` API (without JSX).

**SearchForm**
Refer to the [design prototype](https://www.figma.com/file/fKGjrOqR6nJe6LYJopGCZ8/CDP-Home-Task-%E2%80%93-React-v1), implement a component that renders a search input and a button that triggers a new search.
The component should accept two properties:
Initial search query. Use the value to set the initial value for the input
A "onSearch" callback property. Call the callback property every time the user presses Enter when the input has focus or when the user clicks the Search button. Pass current input value in callback arguments.

**GenreSelect**
Refer to the [design prototype](https://www.figma.com/file/fKGjrOqR6nJe6LYJopGCZ8/%5BCDP%5D-Home-Task-%E2%80%93-React-v1?node-id=0%3A1), implement a component that renders a list of movie genres with currently selected genre highlighted.
The component should accept three properties:
A list of genre names to display. Use the incoming list to render genre buttons.
A name of currently selected genre. Use the name to identify which button to highlight.
A "onSelect" callback property. Call the callback function when the user clicks on any genre button. Pass respective genre name to the callback arguments.

This PR fixes #620 by adding missing block tags to the block tags regex.

Smarty-pants was mangling quotes in the `video` element, which should be hashed by `_hash_html_blocks`, but `video` was missing from `_html5tags` and `_block_tags_a`. Adding it fixed this.

I also added a bunch of other block-level tags listed on [w3docs](https://www.w3docs.com/learn-html/html-block-and-inline-elements.html) such as `canvas`, `dd`, `dt` and `address`

### Update [pytest](https://pypi.org/project/pytest) from **3.6.0** to **8.3.5**.


<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 8.3.3
   ```
   =========================

Bug fixes
---------

- `12446 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/12446>`_: Avoid calling ``property`` (and other instance descriptors) during fixture discovery -- by :user:`asottile`


- `12659 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/12659>`_: Fixed the issue of not displaying assertion failure differences when using the parameter ``--import-mode=importlib`` in pytest>=8.1.


- `12667 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/12667>`_: Fixed a regression where type change in `ExceptionInfo.errisinstance` caused `mypy` to fail.


- `12744 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/12744>`_: Fixed typing compatibility with Python 3.9 or less -- replaced `typing.Self` with `typing_extensions.Self` -- by :user:`Avasam`


- `12745 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/12745>`_: Fixed an issue with backslashes being incorrectly converted in nodeid paths on Windows, ensuring consistent path handling across environments.


- `6682 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/6682>`_: Fixed bug where the verbosity levels where not being respected when printing the "msg" part of failed assertion (as in ``assert condition, msg``).


- `9422 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/9422>`_: Fix bug where disabling the terminal plugin via ``-p no:terminal`` would cause crashes related to missing the ``verbose`` option.

  -- by :user:`GTowers1`



Improved documentation
----------------------

- `12663 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/12663>`_: Clarify that the `pytest_deselected` hook should be called from `pytest_collection_modifyitems` hook implementations when items are deselected.


- `12678 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/12678>`_: Remove erroneous quotes from `tmp_path_retention_policy` example in docs.



Miscellaneous internal changes
------------------------------

- `12769 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/12769>`_: Fix typos discovered by codespell and add codespell to pre-commit hooks.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 8.3.2
   ```
   =========================

Bug fixes
---------

- `12652 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/12652>`_: Resolve regression `conda` environments where no longer being automatically detected.

  -- by :user:`RonnyPfannschmidt`
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 8.3.1
   ```
   =========================

The 8.3.0 release failed to include the change notes and docs for the release. This patch release remedies this. There are no other changes.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 8.3.0
   ```
   =========================

New features
------------

- `12231 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/12231>`_: Added `--xfail-tb` flag, which turns on traceback output for XFAIL results.

  * If the `--xfail-tb` flag is not given, tracebacks for XFAIL results are NOT shown.
  * The style of traceback for XFAIL is set with `--tb`, and can be `auto|long|short|line|native|no`.
  * Note: Even if you have `--xfail-tb` set, you won't see them if `--tb=no`.

  Some history:

  With pytest 8.0, `-rx` or `-ra` would not only turn on summary reports for xfail, but also report the tracebacks for xfail results. This caused issues with some projects that utilize xfail, but don't want to see all of the xfail tracebacks.

  This change detaches xfail tracebacks from `-rx`, and now we turn on xfail tracebacks with `--xfail-tb`. With this, the default `-rx`/ `-ra` behavior is identical to pre-8.0 with respect to xfail tracebacks. While this is a behavior change, it brings default behavior back to pre-8.0.0 behavior, which ultimately was considered the better course of action.

  -- by :user:`okken`


- `12281 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/12281>`_: Added support for keyword matching in marker expressions.

  Now tests can be selected by marker keyword arguments.
  Supported values are :class:`int`, (unescaped) :class:`str`, :class:`bool` & :data:`None`.

  See :ref:`marker examples <marker_keyword_expression_example>` for more information.

  -- by :user:`lovetheguitar`


- `12567 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/12567>`_: Added ``--no-fold-skipped`` command line option.

  If this option is set, then skipped tests in short summary are no longer grouped
  by reason but all tests are printed individually with their nodeid in the same
  way as other statuses.

  -- by :user:`pbrezina`



Improvements in existing functionality
--------------------------------------

- `12469 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/12469>`_: The console output now uses the "third-party plugins" terminology,
  replacing the previously established but confusing and outdated
  reference to :std:doc:`setuptools <setuptools:index>`
  -- by :user:`webknjaz`.


- `12544 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/12544>`_, `#12545 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/12545>`_: Python virtual environment detection was improved by
  checking for a :file:`pyvenv.cfg` file, ensuring reliable detection on
  various platforms -- by :user:`zachsnickers`.


- `2871 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/2871>`_: Do not truncate arguments to functions in output when running with `-vvv`.


- `389 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/389>`_: The readability of assertion introspection of bound methods has been enhanced
  -- by :user:`farbodahm`, :user:`webknjaz`, :user:`obestwalter`, :user:`flub`
  and :user:`glyphack`.

  Earlier, it was like:

  .. code-block:: console

      =================================== FAILURES ===================================
      _____________________________________ test _____________________________________

          def test():
      >       assert Help().fun() == 2
      E       assert 1 == 2
      E        +  where 1 = <bound method Help.fun of <example.Help instance at 0x256a830>>()
      E        +    where <bound method Help.fun of <example.Help instance at 0x256a830>> = <example.Help instance at 0x256a830>.fun
      E        +      where <example.Help instance at 0x256a830> = Help()

      example.py:7: AssertionError
      =========================== 1 failed in 0.03 seconds ===========================


  And now it's like:

  .. code-block:: console

      =================================== FAILURES ===================================
      _____________________________________ test _____________________________________

          def test():
      >       assert Help().fun() == 2
      E       assert 1 == 2
      E        +  where 1 = fun()
      E        +    where fun = <test_local.Help object at 0x1074be230>.fun
      E        +      where <test_local.Help object at 0x1074be230> = Help()

      test_local.py:13: AssertionError
      =========================== 1 failed in 0.03 seconds ===========================


- `7662 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/7662>`_: Added timezone information to the testsuite timestamp in the JUnit XML report.



Bug fixes
---------

- `11706 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/11706>`_: Fixed reporting of teardown errors in higher-scoped fixtures when using `--maxfail` or `--stepwise`.

  Originally added in pytest 8.0.0, but reverted in 8.0.2 due to a regression in pytest-xdist.
  This regression was fixed in pytest-xdist 3.6.1.


- `11797 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/11797>`_: :func:`pytest.approx` now correctly handles :class:`Sequence <collections.abc.Sequence>`-like objects.


- `12204 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/12204>`_, `#12264 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/12264>`_: Fixed a regression in pyt

body:
*Description of changes:*
[sdlf-cicd] split deployment role and codebuild role

This is part of a series of changes to allow both same account and crossaccount CICD for SDLF, and to remove the dependency on seedfarmer - a useful tool but with its own set of problems and limitationsthat are just adding to confusion when people already have to learn how SDLF works.

[sdlf-*] rework sdlf to use nested stacks instead of cfn modules

CloudFormation modules are not available in the Zurich region (`eu-central-2`) and this might be the case in other opt-in regions too... (we also cannot rule out the possibility of cfn modules to be 'de-emphasized' one day, although we have no inside info there)

Cfn modules are used for two purposes in SDLF:
* to package SDLF constructs
* as a UX mechanism, by making SDLF constructs easily deployable as resources in CloudFormation templates

In this PR CloudFormation nested stacks are used instead, relying on some 'clever' use of `TemplateURL`, `{{resolve:ssm}}` and SSM parameter name conventions to keep answering both purposes in a rather similar way.

It's not perfect: seedfarmer is a pain with some symbols (`{{}}`), and aws-sam-cli doesn't like `{{resolve:ssm}}` in TemplateURLs. But it's pretty good... and the following commits should remove the reliance on seedfarmer, as planned.

[sdlf-*] remove seedfarmer dependency

the name is self-explanatory.

author: rahulg321
body:
# Partially Closes #247 
This pull request introduces export functionality to the preview panel, allowing users to download the rendered content in DOCX, PDF, and Markdown formats. This partially addresses the export feature request, as there's a known issue with image rendering in the exported documents.

### Changes
- Implemented an "Export" button in the preview panel.
- Added a dropdown menu to select the desired export format (PDF, DOCX, Markdown).
- Implemented the logic for exporting to PDF using `html2pdf`.
- Implemented the logic for exporting to DOCX using `mammoth`.
- Implemented the logic for exporting to Markdown using `turndown`.
- Added toast messages to notify the user of successful or failed exports.

### Flags
- This PR introduces a core feature for exporting content from the preview panel.
- The implementation covers the most common export formats.
- This partially closes the issue as images within the preview are not currently included in the exported documents. This will be addressed in a future update.
- Toast messages provide clear feedback to the user regarding the export process.

### Screenshots or Video
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e23fc590-ac12-46c0-895b-65d66ede0201

- Issue #247

author: burichh
body:
Hi,

First of all, great notebook! It really gave me an intuitive understanding of the process of flow and score matching. I collected the fixes for the minor issues that I found:

## For `lab_one` and `lab_one_complete`:
1. In my previous PR https://github.com/eje24/iap-diffusion-labs/pull/1 I forgot to change the animation `sigma` value in `lab_one_complete` to `sigma = 0.6`, thus now I added this change.
2.  For both `lab_one` and `lab_one_complete` I changed $D \\triangleq \\frac{\\sigma^2}{\\theta}$ to $D \\triangleq \\frac{\\sigma^2}{2\\theta}$ as that is the variance that the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process converges to.

## For `lab_two_complete`:
**Note**: I only changed `lab_two_complete` for now, just to show what changes I'd add. If they are approved, then I'll apply them to `lab_two` also.

1. I removed the duplications of "arbitrary" distribution definitions, and moved them to the bottom of the notebook, just before they are used. I think this clarifies intention and helps pedagogically.
2. I found some typos in the theorical discussions, missing parentheses, extra nabla and incorrect subscripts.
3. I added some more explanatory labels to the linear conditional path plots.
4. Zewen Yang found a tiny bug and reported in issue [minor error in LangevinFlowSDE class in lab_two_complete](https://github.com/eje24/iap-diffusion-labs/issues/6#issue-2922905538). I added his fix.

## Other notes
These are not part of the PR yet, just notes that I made while going through `lab_two`. I can add them to this PR, or just discard these ideas completely.
1. In the function `imshow_density` it is the _logarithm_ of the density that is being plotted, not the density itself: `density = density.log_density(xy).reshape(bins, bins).T`. I suggest to either rename the function to `imshow_logdensity` or plot the density itself.
2. I found that it would be beneficial to give an intuitive description of the importance of the score $\nabla \log p_t(x)$ in the SDE. Something along this reasoning: The vector field $u_t(x)$ drives the transformation from $p_{init}$ to $p_{data}$. The Brownian motion $\sigma_t dW_t$ is a random noise, that tries to diffuse everything apart. If we only had these two, the transformation from $p_{init}$ to $p_{data}$ would accumulate an increasing noise, as the data points jiggle further away from each other due to Brownian motion. It is the presence of the score $\nabla \log p_t(x)$ that tames the Brownian motion by pulling data points towards the maximum of the log probability, acting against the diffusion! As I was thinking through, I found it helpful to play a bit, like what happens if I remove the score from the SDE, observing the ever increasing jiggling. This can be of course easily understood just by realizing the the score is the gradient of the log probability, thus it pulls the data points towards the maximum log probability (and thus towards the maximum probability, because log is monotonic). I think it might be worth a little paragraph in the notebook to emphasize the intuitive understanding of the terms in the SDE, but it might be it's just me (I'd be happy to write this little paragraph if you think it's helpful:D).

What do you think?

author: soufi
body:
## Fix: Handle console Field as an Object in endpoint Struct

### Issue
Applying a anypoint_apim_mule4 resource in terraform-provider-anypoint fails due to a type mismatch in the console field within endpoint:

```bash
anypoint-client-go: json: cannot unmarshal object into Go struct field Endpoint.endpoint.console of type string
```

### Cause
The API Manager response returns console as an object with two fields (enabled and path), but the Go struct in anypoint-client-go currently expects it as a string:

```json
"endpoint": {
    "deploymentType": "HY",
    "isCloudHub": null,
    "muleVersion4OrAbove": true,
    "proxyRegistrationUri": null,
    "proxyUri": "http://0.0.0.0:8081/",
    "tlsContexts": null,
    "console": {
        "enabled": true,
        "path": "/console/*"
    }
}
```

### Fix
Update the Endpoint struct to define console as a structured object with Enabled and Path fields instead of a string.

## Contributors
Special thanks to: @mitchr

body:
### Description
<!--- Describe your changes here. --->

This PR aims to change how the comparison of SlotWihtIndex behaviors, old behavior would cause some relatively less than desired behavior if two different inventories were comparing with the same index.

This would be a mild breaking change to some degree on servers, however this change should attempt to make the comparison a bit more stricter. Only two areas in skript actually set the raw index accordingly and that's `clicked slot` and `event-slot` for InventoryClickEvent

Everywhere else handles it as `this.index = this.rawIndex = index`

an example of this change being in effect is
```
on inventory click:

Refactored the pie-chart to leave out the timeline slider.  To use there are two new props:

onRoundChanged has one argument which is the new round number.
Remember my rounds are 1-based and the timeline slider is 0-based to you have to adjust.

The other new prop is currentRound is to be set to whatever round the user sets the timeline slider to (+1).

This commit breaks your running demo, but I think you should rework that javascript since I am not confident about how it works.

### Update [requests](https://pypi.org/project/requests) from **2.26.0** to **2.32.3**.


<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 2.32.3
   ```
   -------------------

**Bugfixes**
- Fixed bug breaking the ability to specify custom SSLContexts in sub-classes of
  HTTPAdapter. (6716)
- Fixed issue where Requests started failing to run on Python versions compiled
  without the `ssl` module. (6724)
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 2.32.2
   ```
   -------------------

**Deprecations**
- To provide a more stable migration for custom HTTPAdapters impacted
  by the CVE changes in 2.32.0, we've renamed `_get_connection` to
  a new public API, `get_connection_with_tls_context`. Existing custom
  HTTPAdapters will need to migrate their code to use this new API.
  `get_connection` is considered deprecated in all versions of Requests>=2.32.0.

  A minimal (2-line) example has been provided in the linked PR to ease
  migration, but we strongly urge users to evaluate if their custom adapter
  is subject to the same issue described in CVE-2024-35195. (6710)
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 2.32.1
   ```
   -------------------

**Bugfixes**
- Add missing test certs to the sdist distributed on PyPI.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 2.32.0
   ```
   -------------------

**Security**
- Fixed an issue where setting `verify=False` on the first request from a
  Session will cause subsequent requests to the _same origin_ to also ignore
  cert verification, regardless of the value of `verify`.
  (https://github.com/psf/requests/security/advisories/GHSA-9wx4-h78v-vm56)

**Improvements**
- `verify=True` now reuses a global SSLContext which should improve
  request time variance between first and subsequent requests. It should
  also minimize certificate load time on Windows systems when using a Python
  version built with OpenSSL 3.x. (6667)
- Requests now supports optional use of character detection
  (`chardet` or `charset_normalizer`) when repackaged or vendored.
  This enables `pip` and other projects to minimize their vendoring
  surface area. The `Response.text()` and `apparent_encoding` APIs
  will default to `utf-8` if neither library is present. (6702)

**Bugfixes**
- Fixed bug in length detection where emoji length was incorrectly
  calculated in the request content-length. (6589)
- Fixed deserialization bug in JSONDecodeError. (6629)
- Fixed bug where an extra leading `/` (path separator) could lead
  urllib3 to unnecessarily reparse the request URI. (6644)

**Deprecations**

- Requests has officially added support for CPython 3.12 (6503)
- Requests has officially added support for PyPy 3.9 and 3.10 (6641)
- Requests has officially dropped support for CPython 3.7 (6642)
- Requests has officially dropped support for PyPy 3.7 and 3.8 (6641)

**Documentation**
- Various typo fixes and doc improvements.

**Packaging**
- Requests has started adopting some modern packaging practices.
  The source files for the projects (formerly `requests`) is now located
  in `src/requests` in the Requests sdist. (6506)
- Starting in Requests 2.33.0, Requests will migrate to a PEP 517 build system
  using `hatchling`. This should not impact the average user, but extremely old
  versions of packaging utilities may have issues with the new packaging format.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 2.31.0
   ```
   -------------------

**Security**
- Versions of Requests between v2.3.0 and v2.30.0 are vulnerable to potential
  forwarding of `Proxy-Authorization` headers to destination servers when
  following HTTPS redirects.

  When proxies are defined with user info (`https://user:passproxy:8080`), Requests
  will construct a `Proxy-Authorization` header that is attached to the request to
  authenticate with the proxy.

  In cases where Requests receives a redirect response, it previously reattached
  the `Proxy-Authorization` header incorrectly, resulting in the value being
  sent through the tunneled connection to the destination server. Users who rely on
  defining their proxy credentials in the URL are *strongly* encouraged to upgrade
  to Requests 2.31.0+ to prevent unintentional leakage and rotate their proxy
  credentials once the change has been fully deployed.

body:
I profiled tps demo during gameplay. I noticed that `undenormalize` (called from `Reverb::process` took a substantial role in CPU load.

I optimized the function to reduce total CPU load of tps-demo by about 2.2%.

## Profile Results
The initial profile result on `master` (macOS, `template_debug`):
```
276.00 ms   3,9 %	0 s	  undenormalize(float)
49.00 ms   0,7 %	0 s	  Reverb::process(float*, float*, int)
```
I think the `volatile` keyword is unnecessary, and prevents optimization. I removed the keyword and forced inline of the function (it was already inlined, but it's not a bad idea to have it be inlined in dev builds, too). I profiled again:
```
163.00 ms   2,3 %	0 s	  Reverb::process(float*, float*, int)
4.00 ms   0,1 %	0 s	  undenormalize(float)
```

Flux v2.5.1 is a patch release which comes with various fixes. Users are encouraged to upgrade for the best experience.

Fixes:

Flux v2.5.0 is a feature release. Users are encouraged to upgrade for the best experience.

For a compressive overview of new features and API changes included in this release,
please refer to the [Announcing Flux 2.5 GA blog post](https://fluxcd.io/blog/2025/02/flux-v2.5.0/).

Overview of the new features:

-   Support for GitHub App authentication (`GitRepository` and `ImageUpdateAutomation` API)
-   Custom Health Checks using CEL (`Kustomization` API)
-   Fine-grained control of garbage collection (`Kustomization` API)
-   Enable decryption of secrets generated by Kustomize components (`Kustomization` API)
-   Support for custom event metadata from annotations (`Alert` API)
-   Git commit status updates for Flux Kustomizations with OCIRepository sources (`Alert` API)
-   Resource filtering using CEL for webhook receivers (`Receiver` API)
-   Debug commands for Flux Kustomizations and HelmReleases (Flux CLI)

❤️ Big thanks to all the Flux contributors that helped us with this release!

##### Kubernetes compatibility

This release is compatible with the following Kubernetes versions:

| Kubernetes version | Minimum required |
|--------------------|------------------|
| `v1.30`            | `>= 1.30.0`      |
| `v1.31`            | `>= 1.31.0`      |
| `v1.32`            | `>= 1.32.0`      |

> Backwards compatibility with older versions of Kubernetes and OpenShift is offered by vendors such as
> [ControlPlane](https://control-plane.io/enterprise-for-flux-cd/) that provide enterprise support for Flux.

##### OpenShift compatibility

Flux can be installed on Red Hat OpenShift cluster directly from OperatorHub using
[Flux Operator](https://operatorhub.io/operator/flux-operator).
The operator allows the configuration of Flux multi-tenancy lockdown, network policies,
persistent storage, sharding, vertical scaling and the synchronization
of the cluster state from Git repositories, OCI artifacts and S3-compatible storage.

#### Upgrade procedure

Upgrade Flux from `v2.4.0` to `v2.5.0` by following the [upgrade guide](https://fluxcd.io/flux/installation/upgrade/).

There are no new API versions in this release, so no changes are required in the YAML manifests containing Flux resources.

### **PR Description:**  

**Fixes:** #209    
**Original Issues:** #196 

#### **Overview**  
This PR fixes issue [[#196](https://github.com/mirnylab/cooler/issues/196)](https://github.com/mirnylab/cooler/issues/196) by improving how blacklist BED files are parsed in the `cooler balance` CLI. Previously, single-line BED files, files with metadata headers (`track=`), and empty blacklist files were not handled correctly, leading to parsing errors and crashes.  

The key fixes include:  
- Switching blacklist parsing from custom logic to `bioframe.read_table`.  
- Skipping `track=` headers in blacklist files.  
- Handling empty blacklist files to prevent `np.concatenate` errors.  
- Fixing an HDF5 writing scope error by correcting indentation.  
- Explicitly setting `dtype="float64"` for HDF5 weights to handle `NaN` values.  
- Adjusting test parameters to improve robustness.  

#### **Changes Made**  
✅ **Replaced custom blacklist parsing with `bioframe.read_table`**  
- Previous method failed for single-line BED files due to `csv.Sniffer` assumptions.  
- `bioframe.read_table` now ensures proper BED parsing.  

✅ **Added header skipping for `track=` metadata lines**  
- If the first line starts with `track=`, it is skipped before parsing.  
- Prevents issues where the header was mistakenly interpreted as a chromosome entry.  

✅ **Handled empty blacklist files (`""`) gracefully**  
- Avoided `np.concatenate` errors by checking for empty results.  
- Ensured that blacklist filtering works even if no regions are provided.  

✅ **Fixed indentation issue in HDF5 weight storage**  
- Ensured `create_dataset` operations remain within the `with h5py.File(...)` block.  
- Prevented `KeyError` when writing to HDF5 files.  

✅ **Explicitly set `dtype="float64"` in HDF5 options**  
- Prevented `ValueError: cannot convert float NaN to integer`.  
- Ensured robust handling of blacklist-masked bins.  

✅ **Adjusted test parameters for better stability**  
- Modified `test_balancing_with_blacklist` parameters (`tol=0.1`, `max-iters=1000`, `nproc=1`)  
- Improved test reliability across different platforms.  

#### **Impact**  
- Fixes parsing for single-line BED files, ensuring correctness.  
- Supports blacklist files with metadata headers (`track=`) without errors.  
- Prevents crashes when the blacklist file is empty.  
- Improves compatibility with `bioframe` for BED file handling.  
- Ensures proper HDF5 weight storage, avoiding scope-related errors.  
- Tests now pass reliably, improving maintainability.  

#### **Closes:**  
Fixes #196

author: saryazdi-saman
body:
Resolves #11848 

## Issue
When a payment intent creation returns an indeterminate state (like with StripeAPIError), the payment module doesn't provide a clear way to handle these cases. This can lead to "ghost payments" when webhooks arrive later for sessions that were considered failed.

## Solution
This PR implements a comprehensive solution for handling indeterminate payment states:

1. Add an indeterminate flag to InitiatePaymentOutput type to track indeterminate states
2. Set this flag when providers encounter API errors that should be treated as indeterminate per Stripe's best practices
3. Update createPaymentSession to soft delete payment sessions with indeterminate states
4. Add validatePaymentSessionForWebhook method to properly handle webhooks for deleted sessions
5. Automatically cancel or refund payments that arrive via webhook for deleted sessions

This approach completes the implementation of handling indeterminate payment initiation states while maintaining data integrity.

## Benefits
- Alignment with payment industry best practices for handling indeterminate states
- Improved data integrity by maintaining soft-deleted records for audit purposes
- Automatic prevention of "ghost payments" through webhook reconciliation
- Better representation of the relationship between local records and provider state

Note: I'm happy to help update the documentation to include information about indeterminate payment states  if this approach is approved.
